description: We are Stellar Legion - with obsession on Space Exploration, blending skills in game development, AI and 3D Design. We’re driven to make space concepts more visible, engaging, and inspiring for everyone.
summary: Spacebounds is an authentic, web-playable space mission engineering game developed in Godot 4. Addressing the "Space mission design game" challenge, it turns abstract aerospace trade-offs into an interactive mission lifecycle. In a modular workshop, players balance real constraints: launch capacity, mass margins, internal volume, solar power vs. eclipse battery drain, communications bandwidth, and Delta-V. An automated Flight Readiness Review validates designs against aerospace standards before launch, after which players execute orbital maneuvers, operate instruments, and manage anomalies inspired by the NASA Lessons Learned database. Spacebound is important because it bridges the gap between toy sandboxes and complex aerospace tools. Grounded in official NASA datasets (S3VI, NSSDCA, and Earth Observatory), it democratizes STEM education, allowing students to experience authentic spacecraft engineering.
details:
Spacebounds: Satellite Engineering & Orbital Flight Simulator Game

Project Tagline: Empowering the Next Generation of Space Engineers Through Realistic Mission Simulation and National Heritage.

Play Spacebounds in your Browser:

Here is link 👉 spacebounds

240 Second Video: https://youtu.be/P_-SGncbpRg



The main menu welcomes players with a real-time 3D night scene of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket on the launchpad. Cryogenic vapor vents from the interstage as the vehicle prepares for flight.

Understanding Game Loop

Spacebound simulates the complete engineering lifecycle of real space missions through an authentic and educational gameplay loop:

  1. Contract Selection: Players choose an active mission contract from Mission Control. Each contract specifies target orbits, payload requirements, and budget limits.
  2. Spacecraft Assembly: Players enter the 3D Workshop (Vehicle Assembly Building). They select an appropriate satellite bus and install flight-proven components across all key subsystems.
  3. Engineering Balance: Players balance six critical engineering constraints in real time: mass margin, internal volume, daylight power generation, battery eclipse endurance, maneuver delta-v, and total cost.
  4. Flight Readiness Review: An automated inspection audits the build. Players must resolve all critical warnings before receiving launch clearance.
  5. Launch & Ascent: Players command the rocket from the launchpad. They fly manual or guided ascents, monitor the navball, execute stage separations, and steer into orbit.
  6. Orbital Operations: In orbit, players monitor solar charging and eclipse cycles, perform orbital burns, and downlink mission data.
  7. Debrief & Progression: Successful flights award contract funds and Science Points based on performance, cost efficiency, and design margins. Players spend Science Points in the Technology Tree to unlock advanced hardware for future missions.

Missions

The mission control board features contracts inspired by real Bangladeshi space achievements and regional challenges to inspire the youth:

  • Mission 1 – First Signal (BRAC Onnesha): Recreates Bangladesh's first satellite. Players build a 1U/3U CubeSat, launch to Low Earth Orbit, and transmit beacon signals back home to the Betbunia ground station.
  • Mission 2 – Orbital Sentinel: Focuses on coastal surveillance and maritime protection over the Bay of Bengal using an Earth observation camera and S-band communications.
  • Mission 3 – Delta Flood Watch: Addresses annual monsoon flooding across Bangladesh. Players place a multispectral sensor into Sun-Synchronous Orbit to downlink real flood hazard maps.
  • Mission 4 – Geostationary Gateway (Bangladesh Satellite-1): Simulates the nation's flagship geostationary communications satellite. Players launch to transfer orbit and execute high-apogee circularization burns to park at GEO (119.1° East).
  • Mission 5 & Stretch Missions – Cislunar Pathfinder & Lunar Touchdown: Expands the agency into deep space with lunar flybys, navigation corrections, and powered soft lunar landings.

Workshop


The Workshop serves as the 3D Vehicle Assembly Building. Players inspect their spacecraft on a central payload adapter while the launch vehicle stands in the background hangar. Full orbital camera controls let players rotate, pan, and zoom to examine external instruments, solar arrays, and internal layouts. The interface connects the component catalog on the left with live engineering telemetry on the right.


Component Library

The left panel organizes real-world commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) spacecraft hardware by subsystem:

Subsystems include Power (EPS), Avionics (OBC), Attitude Determination & Control (ADCS), Telecommunications (COMMS), Propulsion, Instruments/Payloads, and Thermal Control.

  • Each component card lists its flight-proven name, dry mass in kilograms, electrical power consumption or generation in watts, and unit cost in millions of dollars.
  • Mission-critical required components are clearly highlighted with a star icon.
  • A search bar and category filters allow players to quickly find suitable parts.

Assembled Payload & Metrics

The right panel tracks the active spacecraft build and displays live engineering matrices:

  • Installed Components List: Displays all attached hardware with quick-remove buttons.
    • Mass: Displays total spacecraft wet mass against launcher payload capacity, showing percentage margin.
    • Volume: Tracks internal liters occupied versus available bus volume.
    • Power: Displays daylight solar generation against subsystem draw to show net wattage.
    • Battery: Tracks total storage in Watt-hours and compares available minutes of power against maximum eclipse darkness duration.
    • Delta-v (Δv\Delta vΔv): Calculates maneuver capability using the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation.
    • Cost: Compares total mission build expenses against the contract budget cap.

Flight Readiness Review

The Flight Readiness Review is an automated quality assurance checklist that prevents costly launch failures. It evaluates:

  • Mass Budget: Ensures total launch mass does not exceed rocket limits and maintains at least a 10% safety margin.
  • Volume Clearance: Confirms internal payload components fit inside the chosen chassis.
  • Daylight Power Balance: Validates that solar panels generate enough electricity to power active systems.
  • Eclipse Endurance: Verifies that battery storage can keep the satellite alive through orbital night.
  • Flight Computer & Sensors: Confirms essential flight processors and attitude sensors are present.
  • Delta-v Adequacy: Ensures propulsion systems carry enough propellant for mission orbital changes.
  • Contract Requirements: Checks that all mission-mandated instruments are installed.

Launchpad

The launchpad scene places the vehicle on the launch pad at the coastal spaceport. The interface provides essential pre-flight telemetry and flight controls:

  • Header: Displays Mission Elapsed Time (MET), simulation time warp controls (1x to 250x), altitude in meters, and an atmospheric depth bar.
  • Telemetry: Real-time readouts track Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR), Mach number, dynamic pressure (QQQ), and G-force loading.
  • Flight Panel: The lower-left staging panel displays engine ignition controls and manual keyboard shortcuts.
  • Flight Guidance: The upper-right banner displays real-time ascent advice and steering hold status.

Navball Attitude Indicator

The Navball provides artificial horizon and attitude guidance for rocket flight:

  • Attitude Sphere: Displays pitch, roll, and heading against an artificial horizon divided into sky and ground.
  • Velocity Readout: Digital display shows surface and orbital speed in meters per second.
  • Heading: Indicates flight heading, anchored at 90 degrees for standard eastward orbital insertion.
  • Flight Reticles: Displays vehicle nose pointing markers and target direction diamonds for precise orbital burns.
  • Flight Modes: Shows active status of Reaction Control Thrusters (RCS) and Stability Augmentation Systems (SAS).

Staging Panel

The staging panel manages the physical separation sequence of the launch vehicle:

  • Stage Hierarchy: Organizes rocket components into sequential stages: Stage 1 booster, Stage 2 upper stage, Payload Fairing, and Satellite Payload.
  • Propellant Gauges: Color-coded bars show real-time propellant depletion for each active engine stage.
  • Safety Prompts: Context-sensitive warnings instruct players to cut engine thrust before releasing empty boosters.
  • Manual Control: Dedicated triggers allow staged separation and fairing jettison with a single click.

Staging Scene in Flight

This in-flight scene captures high-altitude booster separation at 85 kilometers altitude above Earth's atmosphere:

  • The spent first-stage booster cuts thrust and detaches cleanly.
  • The vehicle coasts briefly before upper-stage ignition against a realistic atmospheric haze and planetary curvature.
  • Telemetry shows transition from surface aerodynamic flight to orbital insertion at speeds exceeding 2.0 km/s.

Releasing Satellite to Space

The satellite deploys into Low Earth Orbit at 400 kilometers altitude:

  • The protective fairings separate, and the satellite releases from the upper stage adapter ring into free flight.
  • The user interface switches from rocket ascent mode to orbital operations mode.
  • Orbital telemetry displays circular velocity (7.67 km/s7.67\text{ km/s}7.67 km/s), periapsis altitude (398 km398\text{ km}398 km), apoapsis altitude (400 km400\text{ km}400 km), and eclipse status.
  • An orbital maneuver panel appears on the right for planning prograde and retrograde delta-v burns.

"Connected to Betbunia Ground Station" Alert

Upon deploying antennas in orbit, the satellite establishes its first communications downlink:

  • The HUD flashes a historic green notification: "Beacon received at Betbunia ground station, Bangladesh."
  • Commemorates the historic Betbunia Satellite Ground Station, inaugurated in 1975 as Bangladesh's first satellite gateway.
  • Updates contract status from pending to completed, validating power and communication subsystems.

Flight Debrief

The Flight Debrief screen presents a transparent scoring breakdown upon mission conclusion:

  • Performance Rating: Awards up to three stars and a composite score out of 100 points.
  • Scoring Breakdown: Separates points into primary contract objectives, optional bonus goals, cost efficiency, and mass conservation margin.
  • Settlement: Credits earned contract funds (e.g., $16.00M\$16.00\text{M}$16.00M) and Science Points (e.g., 17 SP17\text{ SP}17 SP) to the agency balance.
  • Unlocks: Announces newly accessible research tiers and contracts.
  • Automated Flight Log: Chronologically catalogs key flight milestones from liftoff, Max-Q, cutoff, staging, and orbit insertion.

Science Points and Funds

The global agency resource bar displays economic standing across the campaign:

  • Funds ($\$$): Represents financial capital used to purchase rocket launches and satellite hardware.
  • Reputation (Stars): Visual star rating tracks commercial and governmental confidence in the agency.
  • Science Points (SP): Academic research currency earned by completing sensor observations, imaging passes, and engineering milestones.

Technology Tree

The Technology Tree provides a non-linear research and development progression across four core aerospace disciplines:

  • Disciplines: Launch Systems, Power & Storage, Communications, and ADCS & Propulsion.
  • Progression: Players spend earned Science Points to research nodes that unlock real spacecraft buses (such as the SSTL-50 microsatellite), larger solar wings, high-density batteries, reaction wheels, and star trackers.
  • Node Inspector: Selecting any technology node displays its prerequisite tree, unlocked hardware, technical specifications, and research cost.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Educational Value: Demystifies orbital mechanics, spacecraft power budgets, and systems engineering for high school and university students.
  • Inspiring National Pride: Highlights Bangladesh's landmark space achievements (BRAC Onnesha, Bangabandhu Satellite-1, Betbunia ground station), demonstrating to young students that aerospace careers are attainable.
  • Critical Thinking & Engineering Trade-offs: Replaces fantasy arcade physics with real engineering decisions. Players must balance mass, power, volume, safety margins, and budgets.
  • High Accessibility: Optimized to run inside web browsers and on standard low-power computers, eliminating expensive hardware barriers for schools and students in developing nations.

Tools, Technologies and Data Sources Used

  • Game Engine & Languages: Godot Engine 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript, WebAssembly/HTML5 export with Compatibility renderer.
    • NASA S3VI SPOON & SSBoK: Small Spacecraft Technology State of the Art reports for verified COTS component specs.
    • NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog: Orbital parameters and instrument packages for scientific spacecraft.
    • ESA eoPortal Directory: Satellite bus platforms and Earth observation sensor specifications.
    • satsearch COTS Database: Industry-standard masses, dimensions, power consumption, and pricing models.
    • NASA Lessons Learned Information System (LLIS): Authentic in-flight anomaly and contingency scenarios.
    • Jonathan's Space Report (GCAT): Launch vehicle capabilities and historical satellite parameters.
  • Geospatial & Planetary Data: NASA Blue Marble Earth imagery, Natural Earth physical vectors, and NASA MODIS flood imagery from the NASA Earth Observatory.
  • Physics Equations: Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Keplerian two-body orbital propagation, AM0 solar irradiance models, and atmospheric drag curves.
